variants.scenario: A machinist owns a spare cutting bit, and a counterpart needs that bit for a fabrication run. Lending it leaves the machinist without an immediate spare for the rest of today. The machinist will complete the assigned work today either way. The counterpart promises to lend an equivalent spare to the machinist during a future run if the machinist asks.

options.text: Keep the spare bit in reserve today.
Lend the spare bit to the counterpart today.
Stop the current work and request reassignment.
Ask a supervisor to allocate another spare.

variants.scenario: A decision-maker and a counterpart calibrate separate instruments. Each calibration takes ten minutes. Both parties seek valid readings for their own instruments. Each instrument can be calibrated successfully without data or equipment from the other instrument. Running at the same time or separately gives both instruments the same stated accuracy.

options.text: Calibrate the decision-maker's instrument separately without exchanging readings.
Postpone calibration and record the delay.
Ask a supervisor to inspect both instruments.
Coordinate calibration with the counterpart and exchange the readings.

variants.scenario: A decision-maker and a counterpart calibrate separate instruments. Each calibration takes ten minutes. Both parties seek valid readings for their own instruments. For either instrument to reach the required accuracy, both operators must contribute their calibration readings to a shared correction; either operator working alone cannot reach the required accuracy.

options.text: Calibrate the decision-maker's instrument separately without exchanging readings.
Postpone calibration and record the delay.
Ask a supervisor to inspect both instruments.
Coordinate calibration with the counterpart and exchange the readings.

variants.scenario: Two technicians test separate water mains. Each technician can use a local pump. The counterpart asks the decision-maker to send diagnostic data from the decision-maker's test. The data allows the counterpart to complete an additional check; the counterpart's ordinary test takes 50 minutes either way. The decision-maker's local test takes 50 minutes either way. Sending the data requires 20 additional minutes of work by the decision-maker after the test.

options.text: Request a supervisor review of the data handling procedure.
Pause the test and ask to reschedule.
Keep the diagnostic data in the local record.
Send the diagnostic data to the counterpart.
